title: Windows Domain Penetration Basics (Assessment-Oriented)
detail:
1. Information gathering: nltest /domain_trusts, net group "domain admins" /domain, SPN scanning (GetUserSPNs)
2. Kerberoasting: SPN service account hashes → hashcat -m 13100 → a primary path for lateral movement in the domain
3. AS-REP Roasting: accounts without preauthentication (-m 18200)
4. Relay: responder poisoning + ntlmrelayx to SMB/LDAP (when SMB signing is disabled)
5. Credential passing: impacket suite (psexec/wmiexec/smbexec/atexec, secretsdump)
6. Golden/Silver tickets: forge after obtaining the krbtgt hash (mimikatz/rubeus)
7. ACL abuse: modify groups with WriteDACL/GenericAll
8. Domain proof artifacts are often found in: DC SYSVOL/NETLOGON, domain admin desktops, AD database ntds.dit (export with secretsdump)
In assessments, the goal is usually to reach "compromise the domain admin and read the proof artifact"; persistence is not necessary.
